advances: An actual two-endpoint-generated source with planar fibers and no new lattice bases after convexification.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
An interpolation at base $z\in[0,2]$ has endpoint weights $1-z/2$ and $z/2$. This proves the complete integer fiber census, and the source is full dimensional. The square is centrally symmetric and has maximum depth $1/2$ by complementary caps. Fact 03bc771bddd39a8a gives the ordinary nonnegative deficits for all three positive planar bodies and the zero deficit of $T$. Thus the square deficit is $\varepsilon^2/18$ and the total is positive.

The polygon $M=T+\varepsilon Q$ has vertices
$$
(0,0),\ (1+\varepsilon,0),\ (1+\varepsilon,\varepsilon),\
(\varepsilon,2+\varepsilon),\ (0,2+\varepsilon).
$$
The list follows by adding the successive edge directions, or by adding the vertex sets and taking the convex hull. Its shoelace area is $1+3\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2$. The enclosing triangle $U=\{x,y\ge0:2x+y\le2+3\varepsilon\}$ has area $1+3\varepsilon+9\varepsilon^2/4$, so its area excess over $M$ is $5\varepsilon^2/4$. At each point of $M$ one barycentric coordinate of $U$ is at least $1/3$. The vertex cap through that point in this coordinate captures at most $4|U|/9$ in $U$ and hence in $M$. This bounds the maximum raw depth in $M$. Scaling area by $1/4$ for $K_1=M/2$ gives $\delta_1\le(4/9)(5\varepsilon^2/4)/4=5\varepsilon^2/36$. Adding the square deficit proves the stated bound.

Minimum enclosing triangles exist for every positive compact convex planar body. Indeed choose one enclosing competitor of finite area. If the body contains a disk of radius $r>0$ about $o$, any enclosing triangle of area at most the competitor contains the triangle from each of its vertices $v$ to the disk diameter perpendicular to $v-o$, of area $r|v-o|$. This uniformly bounds the vertices. A convergent vertex triple from a minimizing sequence remains enclosing, retains the area bound, and is nondegenerate because it contains the disk.

For a compact convex $S$ put $p_T(S)=2h_S(-e_1)+h_S(-e_2)+h_S(2e_1+e_2)$. The family $\mathcal A$ of triangles containing $Q$ with area at most two is nonempty, since $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,2e_2)$ is one. It is compact by the same disk argument with $r=1/2$, which bounds vertices within distance four of the square center. Every minimum enclosing triangle of $Q$ lies in $\mathcal A$. Each support value in $p_T(S)$ is at least its value on $Q$ and $p_T(Q)=3$. If equality held, $Q\subseteq S\subseteq \{x,y\ge0:2x+y\le3\}$. The coordinate segments of $Q$ force the axes to be two facets of $S$, so its intercepts $a,b>0$ satisfy $a\le3/2$, $b\le3$. The corner $(1,1)\in S$ requires $1/a+1/b\le1$. These bounds force $a=3/2$ and $b=3$, and then $|S|=9/4>2$. This contradiction and compactness show $\alpha=\min_{S\in\mathcal A}(p_T(S)-3)>0$.

For each polygon $S$ containing zero the planar Minkowski area formula is $|T+\varepsilon S|=1+\varepsilon p_T(S)+\varepsilon^2|S|$. Here is a direct verification for these polygons. For $\varepsilon>0$, the Minkowski polygon uses the merged edge-normal list of $T$ and $S$, with affine vertices in $\varepsilon$, since each vertex is the sum of the two support vertices at a direction between successive normals. Thus its shoelace area is a quadratic polynomial. Its constant and leading coefficients are respectively $|T|$ and $|S|$, by area continuity at $\varepsilon=0$ and by scaling and taking $\varepsilon\to\infty$. The upper support triangle with the three edge normals of $T$ has area $1+\varepsilon p_T(S)+O(\varepsilon^2)$: translate the two lower intercepts back to the axes and the remaining upper support increases from two by $\varepsilon p_T(S)$. For the lower first-order bound, from each edge $F$ of $T$ choose a support point $s_F\in S$ at its outward normal $n_F$. The swept parallelogram $F+[0,\varepsilon s_F]$ is in $T+\varepsilon S$ because $0\in S$. It lies outside $T$ up to its inner edge, and has area $\varepsilon|F|h_S(n_F)$. Two such parallelograms can overlap only in an $O(\varepsilon)$ neighborhood of their common vertex, since the edge lines meet at a fixed nonzero angle and the strips have width $O(\varepsilon)$. Their overlap areas are $O(\varepsilon^2)$. The edge length weighted support sum is exactly $p_T(S)$, proving the linear coefficient.

The only minimum container of the endpoint $T$ is itself: a proper full-dimensional convex enlargement adds positive area. The other endpoint minimum is $\varepsilon S$ for some $S\in\mathcal A$, by scaling. Regardless of the middle minimum, $(L_\varepsilon)_1$ contains $(T+\varepsilon S)/2$. The preceding area identity and $|S|\ge|Q|=1$ give
$$
|(L_\varepsilon)_1|-|K_1|
\ge \frac{\varepsilon[p_T(S)-3]+\varepsilon^2(|S|-1)}4
\ge\frac{\alpha\varepsilon}4 .
$$
The other excesses are nonnegative and the projection is still $[0,2]$, so this counts actual mixed area without omitted bases. The upper bound on the positive denominator gives the ratio. At each binary layer of the padded hull, every convex combination has to use points in that same layer by extremality of the binary coordinates. Thus both the deficit and the lower cost bound acquire the factor $2^{n-1}$, independently of which minima were chosen in other layers.
statement:
Put $Q=[0,1]^2$, $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,2)\}$, and, for $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let
$$
C_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((\{0\}\times T)\cup(\{2\}\times\varepsilon Q)\bigr).
$$
Its three actual integer fibers are $K_0=T$, $K_1=(T+\varepsilon Q)/2$, $K_2=\varepsilon Q$. For any planar body $K$ write $D(K)$ for maximum ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth. The sum of original ordinary deficits $\delta=\sum_{j=0}^2|K_j|(D(K_j)-4/9)$ satisfies $0<\delta\le7\varepsilon^2/36$. Choose any minimum-area enclosing triangle of each $K_j$ and convexify their lifts at the same bases, obtaining $L_\varepsilon$. There is an absolute $\alpha>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$ and every choice of triangle, such that the actual added mixed area is at least $\alpha\varepsilon/4$ and its ratio to $\delta$ is at least $9\alpha/(7\varepsilon)$. The same ratio holds after padding the source by $[0,1]^{n-1}$ for every $n\ge1$, with arbitrary minimum choices in each binary layer. This family has a source generated solely by its two endpoint fibers and its original middle fiber equal to their Minkowski midpoint.
title: Minimum triangle container cost for an actual Minkowski middle fiber
